excerpt: significance: [p] is (fully) grounded in D only if the connecting questions with respect to [p] and D lack cognitive significance.
overview: The significance principle supplies the first substantive premise in the argument. It links metaphysical grounding to a general epistemic condition: if a connecting question remains cognitively significant even under full information about the relevant natures, the alleged full grounding relation is not present.
title: Significance Constraint
